summary: Halvorsen Coffee Distribution LLC (client) is the exclusive distributor of Brightwater Espresso Systems Inc. commercial espresso machines under a New York-law distribution agreement. Corvane Hospitality Partners has signed a letter of intent to buy all of Halvorsen's membership interests. The partner wants an issue-spotting memo on the distribution package before the deal proceeds. The memo should cover the distribution agreement, Amendment No. 1, the acquisition LOI, Halvorsen's renewal notice letter, and an unrelated warehouse services agreement.

issues.label: change of control consent
issues.description: Section 14.2 of D1 treats any transfer of more than 50% of the Distributor's equity as an assignment. That requires Brightwater's prior written consent, and failing to get it lets Brightwater terminate. The LOI provides for Corvane to buy 100% of Halvorsen's membership interests. Its closing conditions do not include obtaining Brightwater's consent, and nobody has requested that consent.
issues.expected_finding: The proposed sale of all of Halvorsen's membership interests triggers Brightwater's change of control consent right under D1 §14.2. The consent should be obtained before closing and added as a closing condition in the LOI and definitive agreement, or the client risks termination of its core distribution rights.

issues.label: defined term inconsistency
issues.description: D1 §1.1 defines "Products" as the espresso machines listed in Exhibit A. Section 3.1 of Amendment No. 1 sets the annual minimum purchase commitment and redefines "Products" for that purpose as all goods Supplier offers, including spare parts and accessories. Amendment No. 1 prevails under the order of precedence. As a result, the client's minimum purchase obligation, and the related default and termination exposure, now measure against a different and broader product set than its exclusive distribution rights.
issues.expected_finding: Amendment No. 1 uses "Products" inconsistently with the Agreement's definition, and it controls under the precedence clause. The client's $2,400,000 minimum purchase commitment and exclusivity therefore cover different scopes, which should be conformed by a corrective amendment.

issues.label: expired notice window
issues.description: Under D1 §2.2, the Distributor must exercise its renewal option by written notice at least 90 days before the Initial Term expires on December 31, 2026, which means by October 2, 2026. Halvorsen's renewal notice letter is dated October 15, 2026, after that window closed.
detect_terms: hereby exercises its option to renew
issues.expected_finding: Halvorsen's October 15, 2026 renewal notice missed the October 2, 2026 deadline under D1 §2.2, so the renewal option has likely lapsed under New York's strict enforcement of option notice deadlines. Brightwater's written agreement to renew or a waiver should be sought, preferably together with the change of control consent.
